summary: Allows arbitrary scalar expressions in OFFSET (parser, validator, RelBuilder, Enumerable execution, rules, metadata, rel-to-SQL unparsing with new MySQL/SQLite OFFSET-only forms) and renames the FETCH-only validator resources to shared OFFSET/FETCH ones.

tests.evidence: Large feature; offset.iq, JdbcTest, RelBuilderTest, RelOptRulesTest, RelToSqlConverterTest, SqlValidatorTest etc. added; reviewers asked why an existing validator test still passed (fixed by adding a negative-literal check) and for results cross-checked against PostgreSQL.

user_docs.evidence: New user-visible syntax; reference.md updated, but the retained sentence 'start may be either an unsigned numeric literal or a dynamic parameter' now conflicts with the new OFFSET-expression sentence right after it.

doc_comments.evidence: Parser.jj grammar comments, RexUtil.makeOffsetFetchSum Javadoc and RelBuilder.sortLimit @param updated; mostly accurate.

change_description.evidence: Description keeps the full PR template and describes only the parser feature, not the MySQL/SQLite OFFSET-only unparse change, the SortUnionTransposeRule/EnumerableMergeUnionRule changes, or the resource renames; xuzifu666 asked for a summary of why existing tests changed and for a better PR title.

performance.evidence: Planning-time only; no hot loop added.

security.evidence: OFFSET now evaluates arbitrary scalar expressions incl. UDFs, but column references, aggregates and subqueries are rejected; nothing security-relevant beyond a glance.

backward_compat.evidence: Public CalciteResource methods fetchExpressionMustBeNumeric/fetchExpressionCannotReferenceColumn/fetchExpressionEvaluatedToNull (released in calcite-1.42.0) are renamed to offsetFetch* with a new parameter; a negative FETCH literal now fails with a different message; RelBuilder.sortLimit and EnumerableLimit.getExpression change contracts.

error_model.evidence: New validation errors; the same condition now yields two different messages ('OFFSET must not be negative' from the validator vs 'OFFSET value -1 is out of range; expected a non-negative value' from RexUtil), and SqlDialect.unparseOffset throws a bare IllegalArgumentException for non-reducible expressions in LIMIT dialects.

correctness.evidence: Many non-trivial paths: CEIL(offset)+CEIL(fetch) pushdown in union rules, determinism checks for OFFSET re-evaluation, RelMdMinRowCount fallback to rowCount for non-literal offsets, decorrelation guard, parser change from UnsignedNumericLiteralOrParam to Expression.

user_value.evidence: New SQL feature; reviewer questioned scope (author had fixed an unrelated UNION DISTINCT issue and backed it out) and asked to consolidate unparse helpers.

surprising_behavior.evidence: MySQL OFFSET-only now unparses as LIMIT 18446744073709551615 and SQLite as LIMIT -1; documented vendor idioms, but a user reading generated SQL may be surprised.

contradictions.evidence: reference.md now says both that OFFSET start must be an unsigned literal or parameter and that OFFSET may contain any scalar expression; two different negative-value messages for the same rule.

build_ci.evidence: Parser.jj is a grammar source, no build script or dependency change.

observability.evidence: No new retry, fallback, or background state.

spec_conformance.evidence: Extends SQL:2008 OFFSET <offset row count> grammar beyond the standard's simple value specification and emulates it per dialect (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite); reviewers asked for verification against real databases.

plan.why: Large change spanning parser, planner rules and dialect unparsing plus public-API/message changes; logic and contract/docs reviews are independent.
